best_idea: Map a phone stick through a radial deadzone that keeps the stick direction and rescales the length to 0..1, then convert it to a capped per-tic move; the donor's length scale is squared, so fix it by dividing by the length.
decision_why: The radial deadzone and per-tic cap are the input math a phone virtual stick needs; the donor's length multiply is a defect (half throw gives about a quarter of the intended move, 109 vs 438 in the table), so we keep the shape, fix the scale, and expose any soft curve as a client setting.
acceptance: A phone stick held at half throw moves at about 43% of full speed (side 21 of 50), not 25%; a stick inside 12.5% of throw does nothing; a server test asserts that any client move is clamped to 50 units per tic before the engine applies it.
